title: What's New: Going Open Source with the New GitHub Repository for Business Central (2024 release w 2)

chapters.title: BC apps repository launch and statistics
Contribution process: from idea to approval
Setting up development environment and creating pull requests
Pull request requirements and merge criteria
Pull request build phases and testing

features.name: BC apps GitHub repository
features.description: A GitHub repository hosting source code for Microsoft-developed applications including system application, business foundation, and developer tools like test runner and performance toolkit. Launched in November 2023.
caveats: Only hosts Microsoft-developed applications, not for reporting product defects with customer impact

features.name: Community contribution to BC 240
features.description: Community contributors made pull requests to version 240, with 27 community pull requests submitted and 21 merged into the release.

features.name: AL-Go for GitHub automation
features.description: Microsoft's AL-Go product used as the backbone for DevOps to run builds and test applications in the BC apps repository.

features.name: BC artifact version automation
features.description: Automated pull requests that update the BC artifact version in AL-Go settings to ensure builds run against concrete BC artifact versions and development cycles are not broken.
caveats: These are automated pull requests tagged with automation tag requiring no action from users

features.name: App baselines version automation
features.description: Automated updates to app baselines package version used for compiling apps and ensuring no new breaking changes are introduced.

features.name: Translation package version automation
features.description: Automated updates to translation package versions to ensure translations and apps remain compatible.

features.name: GitHub issue templates for contributions
features.description: Contribution process starts with creating an issue on GitHub using one of two templates: either to implement a BC idea or to fix a bug, which triggers collaboration and approval workflow.
caveats: Issues must demonstrate customer non-impact for bug reports

features.name: Pull request approval workflow
features.description: Contributors receive an approved label on their GitHub issue before proceeding with development. After creating a fork and developing, contributors open a pull request which requires two approvals from Microsoft engineers.

features.name: Docker-based development environment setup
features.description: BC Container Helper and Docker-based setup documented for local development environments where developers can publish and test apps with scripts for configuration.

features.name: Linked work items check for pull requests
features.description: Automated check requiring pull requests to link to approved GitHub issues. If no link or unapproved issue, an automated comment explains next steps; linking is resolved by writing hashtag and issue ID.

features.name: Microsoft internal work items tracking
features.description: Automated check for internal Microsoft accounting to ensure release notes and other documentation are updated when changes are made, no action required from external contributors.
caveats: No action items for external contributors

features.name: Pull request build with three compilation modes
features.description: Build phase compiles system application, business foundation, and apps in three flavors: vanilla mode, with translations, and clean mode using preprocessor directives. All must compile for successful merge.
caveats: Clean mode may fail independently while vanilla builds succeed

features.name: Preprocessor directives for clean builds
features.description: Clean build mode uses preprocessor directives like 'clean 23' to exclude specific code snippets from compilation in clean mode while including them in vanilla and translated builds.

features.name: Pull request testing phase
features.description: Second phase of pull request build tests system application and business foundation in both vanilla mode and clean mode, requiring all tests to pass for merge approval.

features.name: GitHub PR debugging with file changes view
features.description: Pull request files tab shows changes and GitHub reports compilation issues inline, allowing developers to identify and fix errors like missing required function arguments without leaving the browser.

features.name: GitHub test failure summary and stack trace
features.description: AL-Go provides a summary of all tests run, showing which ones failed, and displays stack traces to help developers debug test failures.

features.name: BC apps repository contribution process
features.description: Community contributions to BC apps require resolved comments, at least two approvers, linked issues, and passing build checks with no compilation or test failures.

features.name: GitHub contribution help and support
features.description: Contributors can ask for help in pull request comments if they encounter issues during the contribution process, and community members or Microsoft engineers will assist.

features.name: Bug reporting in the contribution process
features.description: Contributors can report bugs in the contribution process using an issue template called 'report a bug in the contribution process' to help Microsoft smooth out the workflow.

features.name: AL development as Microsoft vision for Business Central
features.description: AL development on GitHub represents Microsoft's vision for Business Central application development, enabling co-development with partners and the community.

features.name: Equal contribution requirements for internal and external developers
features.description: All contributors, whether internal Microsoft developers or external partners, must meet the same requirements for pull requests including number of reviewers and passing checks.

features.name: Business Foundation application on GitHub
features.description: Business Foundation is highlighted as the first application developed on GitHub from the beginning, demonstrating Microsoft's commitment to open-source development.
